title: The lead story
content: Google announced a €13 billion investment in Finland over 2027–2028 covering AI/digital infrastructure, energy projects and local partnerships.

title: Why it matters today
content: Google describes the commitment as its largest single investment in Europe, making Finland a major node in the company’s next AI-infrastructure expansion.

title: AI demand is the driver
content: The build is designed to support rising demand for Google services including Gemini alongside Search, Maps and other products.

title: Nuclear is part of the plan
content: Google and Fortum signed a 22-year power purchase agreement tied to the lifetime extension of the Loviisa nuclear plant.

title: The PPA is unusually strategic
content: The contract can cover up to 50% of Loviisa’s capacity during its extended operating period.

title: The deal begins in stages
content: Fortum says contracted capacity starts smaller in 2028 and reaches 50% for 2030–2049.

title: Google is expanding beyond one Finnish site
content: The investment covers infrastructure and partnerships in Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala.

title: Battery storage is included
content: Google has contracted for a new 94 MW battery system near its new Kajaani data center.

title: Wind is part of the energy mix
content: Google says it is adding new onshore wind capacity alongside nuclear and battery projects.

title: This is an AI-and-energy story
content: The announcement links compute growth directly to long-duration power procurement, grid resilience and low-carbon generation.

title: €13B is the headline investment
content: Google says the Finland commitment totals €13 billion over the next two years, 2027 and 2028.

title: Reuters values it at about $15.1B
content: Reuters converted the announced investment to roughly $15.1 billion.

title: Google has been in Hamina for 15 years
content: The company converted a former paper mill in Hamina into a data center and has operated there for about 15 years.

title: More than 600 Finnish suppliers were involved recently
content: Google says its Hamina presence supported an ecosystem of more than 600 Finnish suppliers from 2023 to 2025.

title: Construction impact is projected at over 37,000 jobs
content: Google says the 2027–2028 construction phase will support more than 37,000 jobs nationwide.

title: GDP impact is projected at €3.6B annually during construction
content: Google says the initial build phase will contribute €3.6 billion annually to Finland’s GDP.

title: Permanent employment continues after construction
content: Google says the facilities will support thousands of permanent jobs once operational.

title: Local community investment is €31M
content: Google says it will invest €31 million in local communities in Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala over four years.

title: AI upskilling covers more than 4,400 workers
content: Google says it is partnering with local colleges on AI upskilling for more than 4,400 workers.

title: Student training is included
content: The program includes new training opportunities for 100 Finnish students for future data-center careers.

title: The Loviisa PPA lasts 22 years
content: Fortum says the nuclear power purchase agreement spans the plant’s life-extension period.

title: The contract supports operation through 2050
content: Fortum says the agreement improves the economics of keeping Loviisa operating through the end of its licenses in 2050.

title: Loviisa currently supplies about 10% of Finland’s electricity
content: Fortum says the plant currently produces roughly one-tenth of Finland’s electricity.

title: Loviisa employs about 580 people
content: Fortum lists approximately 580 current employees at the plant.

title: Fortum is already investing about €1B in Loviisa
content: The company says its existing lifetime-extension investment program is approximately €1 billion.

title: Most of the Loviisa extension capex is still ahead
content: Fortum says around €700 million, about 80% of the required capital expenditure, remains pending investment decisions.

title: The PPA improves revenue certainty
content: Long-term contracted demand gives Fortum more predictable cash flow for life-extension investments.

title: Google is not buying the nuclear plant
content: The arrangement is a long-term power purchase agreement, not an acquisition of Loviisa.

title: A PPA links a buyer to future electricity output
content: Power purchase agreements can give generators revenue visibility while giving buyers long-term access to electricity.

title: Data centers need firm power
content: AI data centers run continuously, so operators value electricity sources that are available beyond intermittent weather-dependent generation.

title: Nuclear provides low-carbon baseload
content: Existing nuclear plants can deliver large volumes of low-carbon electricity with high capacity factors.

title: Finland already has a low-carbon power system
content: Its nuclear and renewable generation makes the country attractive to operators seeking lower-carbon data-center power.

title: Cold climate helps data-center efficiency
content: Finland’s climate can reduce cooling requirements compared with hotter regions.

title: Google already uses seawater cooling in Hamina
content: The company highlights seawater-based cooling as one of its long-running Finnish efficiency initiatives.

title: Heat recovery is already part of the model
content: Google says offsite heat recovery from Hamina has been distributed to local homes.

title: AI infrastructure is more than GPUs
content: Large AI deployments also need buildings, substations, fiber, cooling, storage, backup systems and grid upgrades.

title: Electricity is becoming a core AI bottleneck
content: As model training and inference scale, access to power can constrain how quickly new compute capacity comes online.

title: Inference demand matters as much as training
content: Services like Gemini need ongoing compute after models are trained, so operating power demand persists every day.

title: European AI capacity is strategically important
content: More European data-center capacity can reduce dependence on a smaller number of regions and improve regional resilience.

title: Finland is competing as an AI-infrastructure location
content: The announcement positions Finland alongside other Northern European locations seeking data-center investment through power availability and climate advantages.

title: Hamina remains foundational
content: Google’s original Finnish data-center base gives the company an established workforce, supplier network and operational footprint.

title: Kajaani is part of the next expansion
content: Google identifies Kajaani as one of the locations for new infrastructure and energy activity.

title: Muhos is included
content: Muhos is named as one of the Finnish locations receiving investment and partnership activity.

title: Vaala is included
content: Vaala is also part of the announced expansion footprint.

title: Fortum is the energy partner
content: Fortum is the Finnish utility counterpart to the long-term nuclear PPA and broader energy cooperation.

title: Loviisa is the nuclear anchor
content: The Loviisa plant is central to the announced firm low-carbon power arrangement.

title: Google Global Infrastructure leads the build
content: The announcement is framed through Google’s global infrastructure organization rather than as a standalone consumer-product launch.

title: Google’s EMEA energy team is involved
content: The company’s regional energy strategy group is part of the nuclear, wind and grid-integration plan.

title: Fortum’s board-level economics matter
content: The utility says the deal should improve group comparable return on net assets over time once the contracted share reaches 50%.

title: Finland’s government welcomes the investment
content: Prime Minister Petteri Orpo publicly presented the project as evidence of Finland’s digital and innovation strengths.

title: Local colleges are part of the workforce plan
content: Google says local education partners will support AI upskilling and data-center career training.

title: Finnish suppliers gain from the build
content: Construction, networking, operations and service firms are positioned to benefit from the expansion.

title: Grid operators become critical stakeholders
content: Large new loads and generation agreements require coordination with Finland’s electricity system and transmission capacity.

title: Local communities are direct stakeholders
content: The investment includes money for community projects and will change infrastructure demand around host locations.

title: European regulators will watch the build
content: A project of this scale intersects with energy, competition, data-center planning and environmental policy.

title: The PPA starts in 2028
content: Fortum says the nuclear contract begins with smaller capacity in 2028.

title: The 50% level arrives in 2030
content: Fortum says contracted capacity rises to 50% of Loviisa’s output for 2030–2049.

title: The contract supports the full life extension
content: Fortum says the revenue certainty helps enable investment needed to operate Loviisa through 2050.

title: A 10 MW uprate is newly enabled
content: Fortum says the Google arrangement is expected to enable an additional 10 MW power increase.

title: A separate 38 MW uprate was already planned
content: Fortum says an existing 38 MW uprate is expected to be live in 2028.

title: Battery storage adds flexibility
content: The 94 MW battery near Kajaani can help smooth demand and support the grid during periods of stress.

title: Wind adds variable low-carbon supply
content: New onshore wind capacity broadens the energy portfolio beyond nuclear.

title: Google and Fortum signed a wider MoU
content: The companies will explore new nuclear, renewables, flexibility and energy-portfolio-management solutions.

title: New nuclear is on the table, not committed
content: Fortum and Google plan to explore business models for potential new nuclear at Loviisa; no new reactor is yet guaranteed.

title: Powered land could support future data centers
content: The companies will examine whether Fortum sites with grid connections could suit additional Google data-center development.

title: Fortum may also use Google technology
content: The utility says it will explore Google Cloud, AI and data services for its own operations.

title: Grid resilience is part of the design
content: The energy package is explicitly framed around keeping AI growth compatible with a resilient Finnish electricity system.

title: Long contracts change investment math
content: A 22-year buyer commitment can lower uncertainty for capital-intensive power assets.

title: AI demand becomes bankable load
content: Large hyperscaler commitments can turn future electricity demand into a financeable signal for generators and infrastructure investors.

title: Compute and energy planning are converging
content: The deal shows that AI capacity planning increasingly requires simultaneous decisions about chips, sites, transmission and generation.

title: Finland could become a larger European AI hub
content: The investment substantially increases the country’s role in Google’s European infrastructure footprint.

title: Europe gets more hyperscale capacity
content: Additional Finnish infrastructure adds regional capacity for Google services and AI workloads.

title: Nuclear gains another AI customer
content: The agreement extends the trend of major technology companies using long-term nuclear contracts to support data-center demand.

title: Existing reactors may become more valuable
content: AI demand can improve the economics of extending nuclear plants that might otherwise face uncertain post-license investment decisions.

title: Power procurement becomes a competitive weapon
content: Hyperscalers with long-term energy deals may gain an advantage in securing reliable capacity before rivals.

title: Energy availability can shape AI geography
content: Future AI clusters may form where large blocks of affordable, low-carbon, dependable electricity are easiest to secure.

title: Northern Europe gains strategic leverage
content: Countries with cool climates, stable grids and low-carbon power can compete for increasingly capital-intensive AI infrastructure.

title: Finland’s supplier ecosystem can deepen
content: Repeated hyperscale investment can create specialist construction, operations, fiber and electrical capabilities locally.

title: Workforce policy becomes part of AI policy
content: The 4,400-worker upskilling plan shows that infrastructure strategy now includes training, not just hardware.

title: Community acceptance matters
content: Long-term expansion depends on local support around land, power, water, heat, transport and workforce effects.

title: Grid constraints could still slow growth
content: Even with generation secured, transmission and connection capacity can become bottlenecks.

title: Nuclear economics may improve beyond Google
content: If the PPA helps fund life extension, other Finnish electricity users can also benefit from continued plant availability.

title: Battery projects become more important
content: Storage can make very large data-center loads easier to integrate with variable renewable generation and grid conditions.

title: AI infrastructure is becoming industrial policy
content: Deals this large increasingly influence national investment, energy planning, workforce strategy and regional competitiveness.

title: The compute boom is becoming an energy boom
content: The story reinforces that scaling AI is no longer just a semiconductor problem; it is an electricity-and-infrastructure problem too.

title: Watch the 2027 construction start
content: The announced two-year investment window means execution milestones should begin becoming visible in 2027.

title: Watch permitting and grid connections
content: Site construction can only scale as fast as approvals, transmission work and connection capacity allow.

title: Watch whether the €13B plan stays on schedule
content: Large infrastructure programs can shift with demand, supply chains, regulation and financing conditions.

title: Watch Gemini demand
content: Faster growth in Google’s AI services could increase pressure to bring new capacity online sooner.

title: Watch the 94 MW battery project
content: Its commissioning and operational role will show how Google integrates flexible demand with the Finnish grid.

title: Watch Loviisa investment approvals
content: Fortum still has major life-extension capex decisions ahead.

title: Watch the 2028 uprates
content: The planned 38 MW increase and newly enabled 10 MW increment are concrete milestones.

title: Watch the PPA ramp to 50%
content: The contract’s progression toward half of Loviisa capacity is a key commercial milestone.

title: Watch new nuclear discussions
content: The MoU could evolve into feasibility work, financing structures or eventually a project proposal.

title: Watch additional Google sites
content: Fortum-powered land could create options for further Finnish data-center expansion beyond today’s announced footprint.

title: Watch local power prices
content: A core policy question is whether the combination of new load and new generation keeps electricity affordable for other users.

title: Watch Finnish AI employment
content: The promised construction and permanent jobs will be an important test of how much local economic value hyperscale infrastructure creates.

title: Watch supplier growth
content: The number and sophistication of Finnish firms serving data-center, fiber, grid and energy projects should reveal the wider industrial effect.

title: Watch Europe copy the model
content: Other countries may try to pair low-carbon power, grid investment and hyperscaler commitments in similar AI-infrastructure packages.

title: Watch ABC revenue signals
content: For ScrollAI, this story is also a test case: measure whether major AI-infrastructure explainers attract sustained traffic, scroll depth and monetisation better than narrower product-news scrollers.
